body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 21, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 101° and air quality at 108 — unhealthy for sensitive groups. Overnight, a semi truck fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine became the night’s longest-running incident, with crews still working the Tejon fire after 6 a.m. and traffic backing up to the Lebec service route. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the weather, and what’s making news in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident was a semi truck and trailer fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine. Just before 1 a.m., CHP and Engine 56 were on scene, with command established as the Tejon Incident. The fire burned for hours, and by 6 a.m. crews were still working it; a heavy-duty tow had been called in, and traffic was backing up to the Lebec service route. Earlier in the evening, around 10:34 p.m., a quarter-acre brush fire on McCombs Road (State Route 43 north of Wasco) was burning with a fast rate of spread and potential to run west. Multiple engines and a water tender responded, additional wildland equipment was ordered, and crews split into Division Bravo and Division Yankee for what command described as a lengthy mop-up. Around 3 a.m., two subjects were on a Woodford Boulevard property behind a white pickup, possibly taking items. The subjects were known to be in possession of firearms, though none were visible at first; officers later made contact and located a firearm. Around 9:50 p.m., a robbery at gunpoint was reported on Denise Avenue in north Bakersfield. The suspect was described as a transient white male in his late 30s, wearing a baseball cap and black face mask, pulling a wagon, and accompanied by a white female. Around 4:36 a.m., three subjects at a trucking yard south of Gibson Street were reported possibly taking items. Deputies set a perimeter and the subjects ran — one headed south toward a fence with an officer holding the hole. One subject was described as known to carry a knife. Other incidents included a vehicle pursuit running from 30th Street through Union Avenue toward Highway 178, where a perimeter and drone were used, and the driver was described as a Hispanic male, about 56, 175 pounds. A semi truck roughly 50 percent involved with a detached trailer and about an eighth of an acre of grass burning on Interstate 5 in the Grapevine area was reported around 9:47 p.m., with Engine 26 on scene with CHP. A neighbor dispute on Kernita Road following a backyard fire led to officers being asked to back the reporting party. Finally, an attempt to locate the victim of a domestic incident near 17th and Union was reported.

## Today's weather

Today’s weather will see a high near 101° and a low around 74° tonight. It’s currently 99° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County at this time. Air quality is at 108 — unhealthy for sensitive groups. No active fires have been reported beyond the overnight incidents.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Avenal city officials are turning to Arvin as legal issues continue to unfold in the city. The move comes as Avenal faces ongoing challenges and seeks support from neighboring municipalities. **According to 23ABC,** the California Highway Patrol has confirmed new details in the deadly Highway 99 crash from early Sunday morning. CHP confirmed the BMW involved in the crash was the vehicle traveling northbound in the southbound lanes at the time of the collision. Initial reports had indicated the Honda Accord was at fault. All other aspects of the crash remain under investigation, including potential charges. **KGET 17 tells us that** Bakersfield police are seeking the public’s help identifying suspects in a White Lane burglary. **23ABC announced that** NAMI Kern County will celebrate its 20th annual “NAMIWalks” this October at the Park at Riverwalk. The annual event aims to connect local community members with resources for themselves or their loved ones who may be struggling with their mental health. **23ABC also said that** a Foothill High School graduate has won a $25,000 scholarship to attend his dream school. Eric Ventura was awarded the California Table Grape Scholarship after applying last October. After months of waiting, he learned he won the $25,000 award, which will be spread across his four years at UC Berkeley. **Bakersfield Now reported that** a 32-year-old Bakersfield man has died of dehydration tied to heat exposure.

## Something good

Flood Ministries is celebrating its 20th anniversary of providing assistance to Kern County families. The organization has been a source of hope and stability for the local community over the past two decades.

## Coming up this week

This week, several events and meetings are on the calendar. On Tuesday, August 26, a Special City Council Meeting will be held at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. On the entertainment front, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will perform at the Fox Theater on August 22. A Cults & Classics: Season Pass for 2026-2027 will be available at the Fox Theater on August 24. Rodney Carrington will take the stage at the Fox Theater on August 27, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28. Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will both perform at the Fox Theater on August 29.
